name: Engelberg Tunnel
facts: Opened November 5, 1938, the Old Engelberg Tunnel was Germany's first motorway tunnel, stretching 318 metres and pioneering twin-tube design for the Reichsautobahn network.
During 1944–45, Nazi forces converted both tunnels into a Messerschmitt Me 262 assembly plant, employing 3,000 forced laborers from Natzweiler-Struthof, with 374 fatalities.
The 1999 Lower Engelberg Tunnel, 2,530 metres long, sits 60 metres beneath the original, offering a level approach and uninterrupted radio and mobile coverage for commuters.
